answer: Behavioral fingerprint escrow unlock blocks bulk fakes. A new agent locks 500 credits at zero weight. Its walnut record grows twelve epochs before escrow releases. A forge stamping identical sequences across accounts triggers a freeze, since real histories diverge. The named failure mode is script rental: one rented history cannot unlock many identities, since each release needs a fresh fingerprint and lock. The kth fake costs a kth 500-credit lock, so 1,000 fakes tie up 500,000 credits, while one honest agent pays once and recovers its lock as its umber record matures.
